spots.n: Pike Place Market & the Gum Wall
spots.s: The market gauntlet — flying fish, flower stalls and the gloriously gross Gum Wall in Post Alley; Seattle's default great first date.
The 605-ft icon with tilting glass benches and a rotating glass floor — pricey, but worth it once.
Glass fever dream at the Needle's feet — the garden glows at golden hour; date catnip.
The postcard: skyline, Elliott Bay and Rainier from a pocket-size Queen Anne overlook.
Boats rise, salmon climb — hit the fish-ladder viewing windows July–Sept, then stroll the botanical garden; free.
Rusting refinery turned kite hill — THE sunset-over-the-skyline spot across Lake Union.
500 acres of bluff and forest ending at a working lighthouse — the loop trail is the city's best walk-and-talk.
The VW-crushing troll under the Aurora Bridge — five silly minutes that make any date itinerary.
West Seattle's beach strip — skyline views across the bay, volleyball and summer bonfire smoke.
Gehry's purple blob of pop culture — Hendrix, horror props and indie-game arcades.
Downtown's serious art anchor under the Hammering Man — free first Thursdays.
THE cheap date: 35 minutes across the Sound on foot from Colman Dock, wine bars in Winslow, skyline both ways.
Sunset beach with fire pits and Olympic-range views — claim a pit early on summer Saturdays.
230 acres of UW gardens along Lake Washington — Azalea Way in spring is absurd.
1912 glass palm house atop Capitol Hill — pair it with the water-tower viewpoint; cheap and lovely.
Ride the 1914 elevators to a speakeasy-style observatory bar — the smarter, boozier Needle alternative.
Gondolas over Elliott Bay on Pier 57 — touristy, sure, but golden hour up there works.
20 hidden acres of Japanese-American garden artistry in Rainier Beach — waterfalls, moon bridges, zero crowds.
SAM's free sculptures rolling down to the Sound — Calder against the Olympics at sunset.
Wisecracking walk through the buried 1889 storefronts under Pioneer Square — a reliable icebreaker.
Concorde, SR-71 and a walk-through 747 at Boeing Field — the aviation-nerd afternoon that never misses.

nightlife.s: Three rooms of hip-hop, Top 40 and Latin under Pioneer Square brick — Seattle's longest-running big-club night out.
Capitol Hill's big-room floor on a Funktion-One rig — rotating hip-hop, house and EDM nights.
SoDo loft with a rooftop deck — sunset day parties and house sets above the train tracks.
Glittery SoDo disco-warehouse — inclusive crowd, go-go stages, house and hip-hop till late.
Fremont's covered-patio live room — a steady diet of hip-hop, funk and reggae bookings.
Pike/Pine's anchor venue — touring rap and R&B upstairs, DJs and club nights at Barboza in the basement.
The grunge-era legend reborn in Belltown — multiple stages, comedy and late-night hangs.
1939 ballroom steps from Pike Place — the city's best mid-size stage before a downtown nightcap.
Scrappy Madison club mixing rap showcases, dance nights and indie bills.
Beacon Hill's party room — hip-hop and dance nights with pizza slices to soak it up.
White-tablecloth jazz institution since 1979 — dinner-and-a-legend date night downtown.
Plush supper club beneath Wild Ginger — R&B, soul and world acts with cocktails at a booth.
Columbia City's musician-run room — jazz, soul and genre-hopping bills most nights, cheap cover.
A whiskey library of world renown — thousands of bottles and impeccable cocktails for a slow conversation.
Belltown speakeasy down a boiler-room alley — quiet, candlelit, made for a second date.
Rooftop above Pike Place — Elliott Bay sunsets, sharp cocktails and ferry lights for the closer.
Japanese-style private-room karaoke on Capitol Hill — book a room, split some sake, sing badly together.

eats.s: Belltown Edomae temple founded by Shiro Kashiba — sit at the bar and order omakase, period.
Shiro-san's Pike Place room and the city's marquee sushi counter — book a month out for the full omakase.
Ten-seat kaiseki-omakase hidden in a Broadway alley — two dozen exquisite courses; reservations drop monthly.
Ravenna's Edomae sleeper — Tsukiji-trained precision at two-thirds the downtown tab.
Wallingford's beloved no-frills sushi counter — the value play locals happily line up for.
Belltown sushi house with a giant sake list — the late-night happy hour outclasses most full-price menus.
Japantown's 120-year-old izakaya — tatami rooms, black cod collar, pure old-Seattle soul.
Handmade soba and duck from a James Beard-recognized Fremont gem — date-night noodles, elevated.
Serious Tokyo-style ramen born in Japan, grown here — the Capitol Hill shop nails smoky shoyu.
Effervescent Pike/Pine izakaya — small plates, sake flights and a loud, happy bar.
The family that brought pho to Seattle, now in a neon corner shop — brisket bowls and stiff cocktails.
Street-food canteen by Seattle U — rotisserie, vermicelli bowls and strong espresso martinis.
Tiny Lao powerhouse on Madison — laab, sticky rice and chili heat worth the squeeze.
Crossroads-area KBBQ standby — charcoal tables and a proper banchan spread a block from 99 Ranch.
Ballard's jewel-box oyster bar — split a dozen and a glass of Muscadet at the zinc counter.
Filipinx soul food on Beacon Hill — communal, generous and one of the city's warmest rooms.

chinese.s: Old-school Chengdu kitchen on the Eastside — mapo tofu and twice-cooked pork with a real huajiao buzz.
Bellevue Sichuan veterans who cooked in-province for decades — water-boiled fish and dry-fried green beans that taste of home.
The ID's quintessential cart-style dim sum — go early on weekends for har gow and egg tarts.
Hong Kong-style cafe open past 1a — dim sum by day, congee and neon by night.
Cash-friendly wonton-and-congee counter — the ID's best quick solo lunch.
The Bellevue-born xiao long bao chain at its Chinatown-ID outpost — soup dumplings and q-bao without the DTF wait.
The Taipei dumpling empire's first Northwest room at Lincoln Square — precision xiao long bao, every time.
The Sichuan hot-pot giant in downtown Bellevue — table-side noodle dancing and full-service spectacle.
Hand-ripped biang-biang noodles and cumin lamb by UW — Xi'an street food done right.
Taiwanese family kitchen famous for the pork pancake burger — worth the Bellevue line since 2006.
The 1928-founded pan-Asian superstore anchoring the ID — groceries, food court and Kinokuniya books in one stop.
Crossroads' Chinese-market mothership — live tanks, roast duck and every pantry staple.
Pike Place hum bao window since 1979 — BBQ pork buns to fuel the market stroll.
Smithsonian-affiliated museum of the Asian Pacific American story — book the historic hotel tour.

chinese.n: Hing Hay Park 慶喜公園 & Chinatown Gate
chinese.s: The ID's living-room plaza — grand pavilion, ping-pong tables and the historic China gate a block away.
Sichuan-style courtyard garden above the city in West Seattle — a quiet corner of Chengdu with skyline views.
The ID's biggest day — lion dances, Hing Hay Park stage and a 40+ stop food walk; watch CIDBIA for the late-winter date.
One September night of lanterns, food stalls and lion dances on King St — Mid-Autumn energy at full blast.

fishing.s: THE in-city salmon pier — winter blackmouth, Aug–Sep coho and pinks, squid jigging on fall nights; WA saltwater license + free catch record card required.
WDFW's year-round pier north of town — salmon runs, crab in season and winter squid under the lights.
Six-pack charter trolling Puget Sound kings and coho out of Shilshole, minutes from Ballard — license and catch card on you.
40-year Seattle charter outfit chasing salmon and lingcod from Shilshole Bay Marina — gear and coaching included.
Stocked rainbows a jog from downtown — bank and dock fishing year-round with a WA freshwater license.
Smallmouth, jumbo perch and fall coho in the city's backyard lake — launch or bank-fish at Stan Sayres.
Wade the West Seattle gravel for sea-run cutthroat, plus odd-year pinks off the beach; saltwater license applies.
Summer trout water 40 minutes out — swing the Fall City reaches below the falls (freshwater license).
Legendary Sky steelhead and salmon bar water near Gold Bar — check WDFW emergency rules before every trip; catch record card mandatory.

biking.s: Evergreen's flow-and-jump mecca in the Issaquah Alps — pro-built lines from mellow Boot Camp XC to the Voodoo Child jump line.
Big-mountain XC and enduro from the Tiger Summit trailhead — earn 1,800 ft and rip Predator and Off the Grid back down.
The newer DNR network next door to Tiger — Flow State's miles-long descent is worth the whole drive.
12 miles of rooty, rolling singletrack linking Issaquah toward Duthie — the classic lunch-loop dirt.
Techy all-weather skills park under the freeway deck — Seattle's rainy-day dirt fix, minutes from downtown.
Punchy forested loops above Lake Washington on old seminary grounds — bring a Discover Pass.
13 miles of buff beginner-to-intermediate singletrack in the Maltby woods — a great confidence-builder.
The 27-mile paved classic — spin from Ballard's breweries along the ship canal to Lake Washington, car-free.

social.s: The Capitol Hill ballroom's Thursday institution — 9p intro lesson, then a packed, friendly floor till 1a; no partner needed.
All-vinyl salsa on the sprung ballroom floor — old-school mambo energy, beginners genuinely welcome.
Fremont studio's weekly blowout — three rooms of salsa, bachata and zouk after drop-in classes; walk-ins welcome.
Free 6:29a bootcamp with hugs and high-fives — Gas Works in summer, Seattle Center in winter; just show up.

social.n: Green Lake Running Group Evening Run
social.s: Decades-old drop-in run around the lake — 3/5/7-mile options and a chatty pace group for every level.
The Tuesday-night jam running since '97 in a Pioneer Square Irish pub — free, late and full of players.

social.n: Ballard Board Game Night at Mox Boarding House
social.s: Free weekly meetup at Ballard's board-game palace — a new game every 45 minutes and an instant table of strangers.

social.n: Geeks Who Drink Trivia at the Unicorn
social.s: Free seven-round pub quiz in the carnival-themed Capitol Hill bar — join a short team and make friends fast.
Year-round Sunday flea — vintage stalls, food trucks and canal-side people-watching.
The city's best year-round farmers market takes over brick-lined Ballard Ave every Sunday.
Mandarin study-and-chat meetup — low-pressure Chinese practice with fellow learners at ID cafes; locations rotate.
